titles.study_note: Deadpan absurdism; fixed frames and non-professional actors

titles.title: Blood & Water

titles.study_note: Teen mystery with a trafficking thread; Cape Town as a character. Stars Ama Qamata, Khosi Ngema, Gail Mabalane

titles.study_note: 22-episode adaptation of Sue Nyathi's novel; opens at a funeral and works backward. Stars S'dumo Mtshali, Gugu Gumede

titles.study_note: Period epic on the rise of Shaka Zulu; scale of costume, set and battle production

titles.title: DAM

titles.title: Dahomey

titles.study_note: Looted Beninese artefacts returned home; one artefact narrates

titles.title: Four Daughters
titles.recognition: Cannes 2023, L'Œil d'or; Oscar nominee
titles.study_note: Actors and real family members restage the past together

titles.title: The Mother of All Lies
titles.recognition: Cannes Un Certain Regard 2023, Best Director; Oscar shortlist
titles.study_note: Family memory rebuilt with handmade miniatures

titles.title: Touki Bouki
titles.recognition: Cannes 1973, FIPRESCI Prize; restored by the World Cinema Project
titles.study_note: Jump cuts and collage editing; the road movie made African

titles.title: Black Girl (La Noire de…)
titles.recognition: Prix Jean Vigo 1966
titles.study_note: Domestic labor and alienation; the first feature by a sub-Saharan African director

titles.title: Pumzi
titles.recognition: Sundance 2010, short films
titles.study_note: Afrofuturism on a small budget; 21 minutes of world-building

titles.title: How to Ruin Christmas
titles.study_note: Family farce built around a wedding, a funeral and a baby; ensemble comedy timing

titles.title: How to Ruin Love
titles.study_note: Two families' clashing traditions; Season 2 centres on lobola. Stars Sivenathi Mabuya

titles.title: Fatal Seduction
titles.study_note: Erotic thriller where an affair spirals into a murder investigation

titles.title: iNumber Number: Jozi Gold
titles.study_note: The Netflix sequel: a second Johannesburg heist with S'dumo Mtshali returning

titles.title: Silverton Siege
titles.study_note: Apartheid-era bank siege inspired by real 1980 events

titles.title: Queen Sono

titles.title: Kings of Jo'burg
titles.study_note: Crime-family drama in Johannesburg with supernatural undertones

titles.title: Shadow
titles.study_note: South Africa's first Netflix original series; a vigilante who cannot feel pain

titles.title: Seriously Single
titles.study_note: Joburg rom-com about modern dating; sequel Seriously Single Too now streaming

titles.title: Savage Beauty
titles.study_note: Revenge thriller inside a cosmetics empire

titles.title: Kandasamys: The Baby
titles.study_note: Durban family comedy franchise; shot in South Africa and Mauritius

titles.title: The Brave Ones
titles.study_note: Supernatural revenge drama drawing on ancestral myth

titles.title: Unseen
titles.study_note: A cleaner searching for her missing husband reveals a dangerous past. Stars Gail Mabalane

titles.title: Marked
titles.pair_with: The Polygamist (same lead actor and showrunner)
titles.study_note: Stars S'dumo Mtshali; season 2 in production

titles.title: Lobola Man
titles.study_note: Rom-com about Ace Ngubeni, a slick lobola negotiator facing his toughest deal for a shy client; tradition as comic engine

titles.title: The Heart Is a Muscle
titles.recognition: Berlinale 2025, Panorama; South Africa's entry for the 98th Academy Awards
titles.study_note: A father's violent search for his missing son, and the masculinity that drives it; Imran Hamdulay's debut feature

titles.title: Gangster's Paradise: Jerusalema
titles.recognition: Berlinale 2008, Panorama; South Africa's entry for the 81st Academy Awards
titles.study_note: Hillbrow's building hijacks seen from the inside, inspired by true events; Johannesburg's 1990s on a crime-epic scale

titles.title: Nickel Boys
titles.recognition: Academy Award nominee, Best Picture and Best Adapted Screenplay; premiered at Telluride 2024
titles.study_note: Colson Whitehead's novel shot almost entirely in first person by Jomo Fray: the camera is the boys' eyes

titles.title: Capernaum
titles.recognition: Cannes 2018 Jury Prize; Academy Award nominee, Best Foreign Language Film
titles.study_note: A non-professional cast found on Beirut's streets, filmed at a child's eye level over months to catch real behaviour

titles.title: The Wizard of Oz
titles.recognition: Academy Awards for Best Original Song and Best Original Score
titles.study_note: Sepia Kansas gives way to three-strip Technicolor Oz: colour as the story's turning point

titles.title: Citizen Kane
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay
titles.pair_with: The Mother of All Lies (El Moudir)
titles.study_note: Gregg Toland's deep focus and low angles; a life pieced together from other people's memories
titles.essential: It topped Sight and Sound's critics' poll for 50 years: the shorthand for an ambitious debut and for deep-focus craft.

titles.title: The Maltese Falcon
titles.recognition: Three Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture
titles.study_note: Hard-boiled dialogue and low-key light that set the pattern for film noir

titles.title: Casablanca
titles.recognition: Academy Awards for Best Picture, Director and Screenplay
titles.study_note: A studio-built Morocco, shadowed close-ups and a script rewritten during the shoot
titles.essential: The model studio-system picture: written while it was shot, endlessly quoted, still the reference for romance on screen.

titles.title: It's a Wonderful Life
titles.recognition: Five Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture
titles.study_note: A whole town's life told in flashback, on a snowbound set built for a summer shoot

titles.title: All About Eve
titles.recognition: Six Academy Awards from 14 nominations, including Best Picture and Director
titles.study_note: A backstage rivalry carried by dialogue and several voice-over narrators

titles.title: Sunset Boulevard
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Story and Screenplay
titles.study_note: Hollywood looking at itself: a dead narrator, a forgotten silent star and a decaying mansion
titles.essential: Hollywood's own warning about fame and the studio machine; its last line is one of the most quoted.

titles.title: Singin' in the Rain
titles.recognition: Two Academy Award nominations
titles.study_note: Dance staged for the camera; the move from silent films to sound played as comedy
titles.essential: The industry laughing at itself over the arrival of sound: the musical everyone in the room has seen.

titles.title: Roman Holiday
titles.recognition: Academy Awards for Best Actress (Audrey Hepburn) and Best Story
titles.study_note: Shot on location in Rome, rare for a studio picture of its time

titles.title: On the Waterfront
titles.recognition: Eight Academy Awards, including Best Picture, Director and Actor (Marlon Brando)
titles.study_note: Method acting on the real Hoboken docks; the taxi-cab scene

titles.title: Carmen Jones
titles.recognition: Dorothy Dandridge became the first Black woman nominated for the Academy Award for Best Actress
titles.study_note: Bizet's opera reset with an all-Black cast, in CinemaScope colour

titles.title: Rebel Without a Cause
titles.recognition: Three Academy Award nominations
titles.study_note: Wide CinemaScope colour turned on teenage anguish; James Dean's defining role

titles.title: The Searchers
titles.recognition: Named the greatest American western by the American Film Institute (2008)
titles.study_note: Monument Valley in VistaVision; the doorway shots that open and close the film

titles.title: Vertigo
titles.recognition: Voted the greatest film of all time in Sight and Sound's 2012 critics' poll
titles.study_note: The dolly zoom; colour, especially green, as obsession; Saul Bass's titles
titles.essential: It replaced Citizen Kane at the top of Sight and Sound's poll in 2012: the film people mean when they talk about Hitchcock's craft.

titles.title: Some Like It Hot
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Costume Design
titles.study_note: Shot in black and white so the drag make-up would read; comic timing held in long takes

titles.title: Imitation of Life
titles.recognition: Academy Award nominations for Juanita Moore and Susan Kohner
titles.study_note: Melodrama as social critique: colour, mirrors and a funeral finale

titles.title: Psycho
titles.recognition: Four Academy Award nominations
titles.study_note: Killing off the star halfway through; the shower scene's rapid cutting and Bernard Herrmann's strings
titles.essential: Made cheaply with a TV crew and sold with a no-late-admission rule: proof that marketing and craft can turn a small film into an event.

titles.title: West Side Story
titles.recognition: Ten Academy Awards, including Best Picture
titles.study_note: Gang conflict as dance on real New York streets; colour-coded light

titles.title: Lawrence of Arabia
titles.recognition: Seven Academy Awards, including Best Picture and Director
titles.study_note: Desert vistas in Super Panavision 70; the cut from a blown-out match to the sunrise

titles.title: To Kill a Mockingbird
titles.recognition: Academy Awards for Best Actor (Gregory Peck) and Adapted Screenplay
titles.study_note: A novel adapted through a child's eyes; the courtroom as the film's moral centre

titles.title: In the Heat of the Night
titles.recognition: Academy Awards for Best Picture and Best Actor (Rod Steiger)
titles.study_note: Racial tension built into a murder procedural; Haskell Wexler's lighting for Sidney Poitier

titles.title: The Graduate
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Director
titles.study_note: Long lenses that trap Benjamin in the frame; Simon & Garfunkel songs as narration

titles.title: Bonnie and Clyde
titles.recognition: Academy Awards for Best Supporting Actress (Estelle Parsons) and Cinematography
titles.study_note: New Hollywood's break with the old code: violence, sex and abrupt editing

titles.title: 2001: A Space Odyssey
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Visual Effects
titles.study_note: Front projection, practical effects and long silences; the bone-to-satellite match cut
titles.essential: The reference point for practical visual effects and for trusting an audience with silence.

titles.title: The Godfather
titles.recognition: Academy Awards for Best Picture, Actor (Marlon Brando) and Adapted Screenplay
titles.study_note: Gordon Willis's top-lit darkness; the baptism cross-cut with the killings
titles.essential: The yardstick for adaptation and ensemble casting, and for the fight between a director and his studio that New Hollywood was made of.

titles.title: Jaws
titles.recognition: Three Academy Awards (editing, score and sound); the first summer blockbuster
titles.study_note: A broken mechanical shark turned into suspense: the threat mostly unseen, John Williams's two notes
titles.essential: It invented the summer blockbuster: a wide release backed by national TV advertising, the plan most tentpole releases still follow.

titles.title: Taxi Driver
titles.recognition: Palme d'Or, Cannes 1976
titles.study_note: New York at night through a disturbed narrator; Bernard Herrmann's last score

titles.title: Network
titles.recognition: Four Academy Awards, three of them for acting
titles.study_note: Paddy Chayefsky's satire of television, delivered in long, theatrical speeches
titles.essential: Its predictions about television news are quoted in every conversation about media; 'mad as hell' is part of the vocabulary.

titles.title: Star Wars
titles.recognition: Six Academy Awards
titles.study_note: A lived-in, used-future world built from models, production design and sound design
titles.essential: George Lucas kept the sequel and merchandising rights: it turned merchandise into the business model and changed how deals are made.

titles.title: Apocalypse Now
titles.recognition: Palme d'Or, Cannes 1979
titles.pair_with: Sew the Winter to My Skin (Qubeka)
titles.study_note: A troubled shoot in the Philippines; Vittorio Storaro's colour and Walter Murch's sound design
titles.essential: The cautionary tale of a shoot running out of control, retold in the documentary Hearts of Darkness.

titles.title: Ride Along
titles.recognition: Number one at the US box office on its opening weekend
titles.study_note: Buddy-comedy chemistry between Ice Cube and Kevin Hart; comic timing inside action set pieces

titles.title: The Matrix
titles.recognition: Four Academy Awards, including Best Visual Effects
titles.study_note: Bullet time, Yuen Woo-ping's wire-work fights and a green-tinted digital world
titles.essential: Bullet time, the Wachowskis' world-building and a franchise blueprint: still the reference in action and visual-effects pitches.

titles.title: Coming to America
titles.recognition: Two Academy Award nominations (costume design and make-up)
titles.study_note: Eddie Murphy and Arsenio Hall in several roles each under Rick Baker's make-up

titles.title: Coming 2 America
titles.recognition: Academy Award nomination for Best Makeup and Hairstyling
titles.study_note: Ruth E. Carter's costumes bring Zamunda back in colour; a legacy sequel built on its returning cast

titles.title: The Karate Kid
titles.recognition: Over $350 million worldwide
titles.study_note: The remake moved to Beijing: Jackie Chan's dramatic turn and training scenes shot on location in China

titles.title: The Pursuit of Happyness
titles.recognition: Academy Award nomination for Best Actor (Will Smith)
titles.study_note: A true story played close to the ground; Will Smith opposite his son Jaden

titles.title: Do the Right Thing
titles.recognition: Academy Award nominations for Best Original Screenplay and Supporting Actor (Danny Aiello)
titles.study_note: Ernest Dickerson's heat-soaked colour, tilted angles and a single Brooklyn block
titles.essential: Spike Lee's breakthrough, on every list of essential American films; the reference for colour, heat and point of view.

titles.title: Boyz n the Hood
titles.recognition: John Singleton became the youngest person and the first Black director nominated for Best Director
titles.study_note: Coming of age in South Central Los Angeles; a debut written from life

titles.title: Malcolm X
titles.recognition: Academy Award nominations for Best Actor (Denzel Washington) and Costume Design
titles.study_note: A three-hour epic biopic: Ruth E. Carter's costumes and Denzel Washington's transformation

titles.title: Training Day
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Actor (Denzel Washington)
titles.study_note: One day in a car with a corrupt detective; Denzel Washington cast against type

titles.title: Ray
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Actor (Jamie Foxx)
titles.study_note: A music biopic built on Jamie Foxx's performance and Ray Charles's own recordings

titles.title: Dreamgirls
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress (Jennifer Hudson)
titles.study_note: A Broadway musical brought to the screen, with performances staged after the Motown era

titles.title: Bad Boys
titles.recognition: The start of a four-film franchise
titles.study_note: Will Smith and Martin Lawrence improvising inside glossy, fast-cut action

titles.title: Waiting to Exhale
titles.recognition: Adapted from Terry McMillan's best-selling novel
titles.study_note: Four friends' lives in parallel; an ensemble led by Whitney Houston and Angela Bassett

titles.title: Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon
titles.recognition: Four Academy Awards, including Best Foreign Language Film
titles.study_note: Yuen Woo-ping's wire-work; fights staged like dance in the bamboo treetops

titles.title: Get Out
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay
titles.study_note: Social horror built from everyday racism; the Sunken Place
titles.essential: A $4.5 million film that took over $250 million and won Best Original Screenplay: the model for genre with something to say.

titles.title: Black Panther
titles.recognition: Three Academy Awards (costume design, production design and score)
titles.study_note: Afrofuturist world-building: Ruth E. Carter's costumes and Hannah Beachler's production design
titles.essential: Over $1.3 billion worldwide and the first superhero film nominated for Best Picture: it ended the argument about Black-led blockbusters.

titles.title: Moonlight
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Picture
titles.study_note: One life in three chapters played by three actors; James Laxton's saturated Miami colour
titles.essential: A Best Picture winner made for about $4 million, and the envelope mix-up at the Oscars made it a story everyone tells.

titles.title: Hidden Figures
titles.recognition: Three Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture
titles.study_note: The true story of the Black women mathematicians behind NASA's early space flights

titles.title: Crazy Rich Asians
titles.recognition: The first major Hollywood studio film with a majority Asian cast in 25 years
titles.study_note: A romantic comedy staged as spectacle in Singapore; casting and costume as world-building

titles.title: Rocky
titles.recognition: Academy Awards for Best Picture and Director
titles.study_note: Made for about $1 million; the training montage and the museum steps shot with an early Steadicam
titles.essential: Sylvester Stallone wouldn't sell his script unless he starred in it: the story every writer-actor hears about betting on yourself.

titles.title: The Godfather Part II
titles.recognition: Academy Awards for Best Picture, Director and Supporting Actor (Robert De Niro)
titles.study_note: A sequel and a prequel cut together: two timelines in parallel
titles.essential: The first sequel to win Best Picture: the answer whenever someone says sequels can't be art.

titles.title: Back to the Future
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Sound Effects Editing
titles.study_note: Every scene sets up a payoff; Michael J. Fox replaced the original lead weeks into the shoot
titles.essential: Taught in screenwriting classes for its setups and payoffs: nothing on screen is wasted.

titles.title: Die Hard
titles.recognition: Four Academy Award nominations
titles.study_note: One building as the whole world; the hero as an ordinary man
titles.essential: 'Die Hard on a…' is how countless action films are pitched: the template for a contained, single-location thriller.

titles.title: Jurassic Park
titles.recognition: Three Academy Awards, including Best Visual Effects
titles.study_note: Stan Winston's animatronics alongside Industrial Light & Magic's computer-generated dinosaurs
titles.essential: The turning point from practical effects to computer-generated creatures, made by blending both.

titles.title: Pulp Fiction
titles.recognition: Palme d'Or, Cannes 1994, and the Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay
titles.study_note: Chapters told out of order; long, dialogue-led scenes
titles.essential: Won the Palme d'Or and turned an independent film into a box-office hit: the reference for non-linear structure and dialogue.

titles.title: The Shawshank Redemption
titles.recognition: Seven Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture
titles.study_note: Roger Deakins's restrained photography; a voice-over carrying a decades-long story
titles.essential: It disappointed at the box office, then became beloved on home video and TV: the case study for a film's second life.

titles.title: Toy Story
titles.recognition: A Special Achievement Academy Award as the first feature-length computer-animated film
titles.study_note: Characters designed around what computers could render; story first
titles.essential: The first fully computer-animated feature; its story-first process is still copied by studios.

titles.title: Titanic
titles.recognition: Eleven Academy Awards, including Best Picture
titles.study_note: A near-full-scale ship built in a tank in Mexico; spectacle carried by a love story
titles.essential: It ran far over budget with the industry predicting disaster, then became the highest-grossing film of its time.

titles.title: The Blair Witch Project
titles.recognition: Made for a reported $60,000; it earned about $248 million
titles.study_note: Found footage shot by the actors themselves; largely improvised performances
titles.essential: Sold through an early internet campaign that blurred fact and fiction: the case study in viral marketing.

titles.title: Gone with the Wind
titles.recognition: Eight Academy Awards, including Best Picture; Hattie McDaniel became the first Black actor to win an Oscar
titles.study_note: Technicolor at epic scale: firelit night scenes and burnt-orange skies. Study it with its romanticised view of slavery in mind
titles.essential: Still the biggest box-office film once prices are adjusted, and the reference point for Technicolor spectacle and for how Hollywood romanticised the Old South.

titles.title: Double Indemnity
titles.recognition: Seven Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture
titles.study_note: The film noir template: venetian-blind shadows, a voice-over confession and a scheme that goes wrong
titles.essential: The noir that crime writers and DPs still borrow from: told backwards from a confession and lit through venetian blinds.

titles.title: Rear Window
titles.recognition: Four Academy Award nominations, including Best Director
titles.study_note: One courtyard set and one point of view: suspense built from what the camera, and the audience, can see
titles.essential: Hitchcock's lesson in point of view and suspense, shot from one apartment on one enormous studio set.

titles.title: North by Northwest
titles.recognition: Three Academy Award nominations
titles.study_note: The chase-film blueprint: a crop-duster attack in open daylight, Saul Bass's opening titles and a Mount Rushmore finale
titles.essential: The template for the spy chase film; the crop-duster scene is the reference for suspense in broad daylight.

titles.title: It Happened One Night
titles.recognition: The first film to win all five top Academy Awards: picture, director, actor, actress and screenplay
titles.study_note: The screwball road comedy: sparring leads, quick dialogue and a bus trip that turns into a romance
titles.essential: The first film to sweep the five top Oscars, and the template the romantic comedy still follows.

titles.title: The Grapes of Wrath
titles.recognition: Academy Awards for Best Director and Best Supporting Actress
titles.study_note: Gregg Toland's deep-focus black and white turns Dust Bowl migration into images that look like documentary photographs

titles.title: Mildred Pierce
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Actress (Joan Crawford)
titles.study_note: Noir lighting around a mother-and-daughter melodrama, told in flashback from a murder

titles.title: Sunrise: A Song of Two Humans
titles.recognition: Three Academy Awards at the first ceremony, including Unique and Artistic Production
titles.study_note: German expressionism inside a Hollywood studio: forced-perspective city sets, superimpositions and a camera that moves, with no dialogue

titles.title: Ben-Hur
titles.recognition: 11 Academy Awards, a record later matched by Titanic and The Return of the King
titles.study_note: The chariot race: months of second-unit work, a vast arena set and widescreen staging that action films still study
titles.essential: The chariot race is still the benchmark for practical action at scale, and its 11 Oscars are still the record.

titles.title: Paths of Glory
titles.recognition: Not shown in France until 1975
titles.study_note: Kubrick's long tracking shots through the trenches, set against a château where the generals decide who dies

titles.title: 12 Angry Men
titles.recognition: Three Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture
titles.study_note: One room, twelve actors, close to real time: the lenses get longer and the camera lower as the pressure rises
titles.essential: The model for drama in a single room: Lumet shoots it with longer lenses and a lower camera as the tension builds.

titles.title: City Lights
titles.study_note: Chaplin kept it silent after sound arrived: physical comedy, his own score and a final close-up that does the work of dialogue
titles.essential: Chaplin's silent comedy made after sound took over; its last close-up is taught as one of the great endings.

titles.title: Footlight Parade
titles.study_note: Busby Berkeley's overhead kaleidoscope numbers: choreography designed for the camera, not the stage

titles.title: Out of the Past
titles.recognition: Added to the National Film Registry in 1991
titles.study_note: Nicholas Musuraca's noir lighting and a flashback plot about a man who can't outrun his past

titles.title: Rebecca
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Picture, the only Hitchcock film to win it
titles.study_note: A house as the antagonist: a dead woman who never appears fills every room through the sets, the shadows and the housekeeper

titles.title: Seven Samurai
titles.recognition: Silver Lion at the Venice Film Festival
titles.study_note: Several cameras, long lenses, mud and rain: battle staged in weather, with the team gathered one man at a time
titles.essential: The source of the gather-the-team story, from The Magnificent Seven to heist films, and the reference for staging battle in weather.

titles.title: I Am a Fugitive from a Chain Gang
titles.recognition: Three Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture
titles.study_note: Warner Bros.' social realism before the Production Code: a true story that helped end the chain gangs, with a famously dark last line

titles.title: The Ox-Bow Incident
titles.recognition: Nominated for the Academy Award for Best Picture
titles.study_note: A western without heroes: a lynch mob over a single day, shot mostly on soundstages

titles.title: The Shop Around the Corner
titles.recognition: Added to the National Film Registry in 1999
titles.study_note: The Lubitsch touch: two shop clerks who can't stand each other are each other's pen pals, almost all on one shop set

titles.title: Trouble in Paradise
titles.recognition: Added to the National Film Registry in 1991
titles.study_note: Pre-Code sophistication: two thieves in love, told through doors, clocks and what the camera leaves out

titles.title: Stormy Weather
titles.recognition: Added to the National Film Registry in 2001
titles.study_note: A studio musical with an all-Black cast built around Lena Horne, Bill Robinson and Cab Calloway; the Nicholas Brothers' stair-leaping finale is still studied by choreographers
titles.essential: The Nicholas Brothers' finale is one of the most referenced dance numbers ever filmed.

titles.title: Cabin in the Sky
titles.recognition: Nominated for the Academy Award for Best Original Song
titles.study_note: Minnelli's first feature: an all-Black musical fable with Ethel Waters, Lena Horne and Louis Armstrong, made inside MGM's studio system

titles.title: The Emperor Jones
titles.study_note: Paul Robeson in Eugene O'Neill's play, billed above his white co-stars in 1933: the rise and fall of a Pullman porter who makes himself an island's ruler

titles.title: Porgy and Bess
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Scoring of a Musical Picture
titles.study_note: Goldwyn's widescreen Todd-AO version of the Gershwin opera with Sidney Poitier, Dorothy Dandridge and Sammy Davis Jr., rarely seen since the Gershwin estate withdrew it

titles.title: A Raisin in the Sun
titles.recognition: Gary Cooper Award at the Cannes Film Festival
titles.study_note: Lorraine Hansberry's play with most of its Broadway cast: a Chicago family in one cramped apartment, the drama built from close quarters
titles.essential: Lorraine Hansberry's story of a Black family's dream of a house is a cornerstone of American drama, and one of Sidney Poitier's defining roles.

titles.title: Imitation of Life (1934)
titles.recognition: Nominated for the Academy Award for Best Picture
titles.study_note: The first version of Fannie Hurst's story, in which Louise Beavers' and Fredi Washington's storyline about race and passing outweighs the star's

titles.title: Lilies of the Field
titles.recognition: Sidney Poitier became the first Black man to win the Academy Award for Best Actor
titles.study_note: A small, warm film shot in about two weeks in Arizona, carried by Poitier and a handful of nuns
titles.essential: Sidney Poitier's Best Actor Oscar, the first for a Black man, comes up in every history of the industry.

titles.title: The Blood of Jesus
titles.recognition: Added to the National Film Registry in 1991
titles.study_note: A race film made for a few thousand dollars with a Texas church congregation in the cast, and one of the most successful of its time

titles.title: Native Son (1951)
titles.study_note: Richard Wright plays Bigger Thomas in the film of his own novel, shot in Argentina when no US studio would make it as written

titles.title: The Joe Louis Story
titles.study_note: A boxing biopic that cuts Joe Louis's real fight footage into the drama, with Coley Wallace as Louis

titles.title: The General
titles.recognition: Added to the National Film Registry in 1989
titles.study_note: Keaton's locomotive chase done for real: full-size trains, a real bridge collapse and stunts with no doubles
titles.essential: The benchmark for physical comedy and practical stunt work; Keaton did it all for real.

titles.title: Modern Times
titles.recognition: Added to the National Film Registry in 1989
titles.study_note: Chaplin's farewell to the Tramp: the factory and the machine played as comedy, almost without dialogue a decade into sound

titles.title: King Kong
titles.credit: Merian C. Cooper & Ernest B. Schoedsack
titles.recognition: Added to the National Film Registry in 1991
titles.study_note: Willis O'Brien's stop-motion ape and miniatures: the effects film that set the template for the monster blockbuster
titles.essential: The ancestor of the effects blockbuster; Willis O'Brien's stop-motion is where the history of screen effects starts.

titles.title: Frankenstein
titles.recognition: Added to the National Film Registry in 1991
titles.study_note: Jack Pierce's make-up and Boris Karloff's performance defined the screen monster, on expressionist sets built on Universal's lot

titles.title: His Girl Friday
titles.recognition: Added to the National Film Registry in 1993
titles.study_note: Dialogue at record speed: Hawks had the cast talk over each other and shot it in long, crowded takes
titles.essential: The reference for fast, overlapping dialogue in comedy.

titles.title: Stagecoach
titles.recognition: Two Academy Awards, including Best Supporting Actor (Thomas Mitchell)
titles.study_note: Ford's first Monument Valley western: nine strangers in one coach, and the shot that made John Wayne a star
titles.essential: The western Orson Welles said he watched some forty times while preparing Citizen Kane.

titles.title: Notorious
titles.recognition: Two Academy Award nominations
titles.study_note: A crane shot from a whole party down to the key in Ingrid Bergman's hand, and a kiss broken up to get round the censors' time limit

titles.title: Touch of Evil
titles.recognition: Added to the National Film Registry in 1993
titles.study_note: The opening crane shot, more than three minutes without a cut, and border-town noir shot at night in Venice, California
titles.essential: Its opening long take is the one cinematography classes still show first.

titles.title: High Noon
titles.recognition: Four Academy Awards, including Best Actor (Gary Cooper)
titles.study_note: A western told in close to real time, clocks in shot, in a flat, harsh light that suits its blacklist-era story

titles.title: The Night of the Hunter
titles.recognition: Added to the National Film Registry in 1992
titles.study_note: Laughton's only film as director: silent-era expressionism, a river journey shot like a fairy tale and Robert Mitchum's tattooed hands

titles.title: Bride of Frankenstein
titles.recognition: Added to the National Film Registry in 1998
titles.study_note: Whale's sequel goes further than the original: camp, pathos and the Bride's hair and make-up, on screen for a few minutes and an icon ever since

titles.title: Laura
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Cinematography (Joseph LaShelle)
titles.study_note: A detective falls for a murdered woman's portrait: Preminger's gliding camera and David Raksin's theme carry the obsession

titles.title: Gilda
titles.recognition: Added to the National Film Registry in 2013
titles.study_note: Rita Hayworth's entrance and "Put the Blame on Mame": how a star is lit and framed to own every scene she's in

titles.title: The African Queen
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Actor (Humphrey Bogart)
titles.study_note: Shot largely on location in Uganda and the Belgian Congo in Technicolor, with Bogart and Hepburn mostly on one small boat

titles.title: The Adventures of Robin Hood
titles.recognition: Three Academy Awards, including Best Original Score
titles.study_note: Three-strip Technicolor at its boldest, Erich Wolfgang Korngold's score and the swordfight fought in shadow on the castle wall

titles.title: Bringing Up Baby
titles.recognition: Added to the National Film Registry in 1990
titles.study_note: Screwball comedy at full speed: Hepburn, Grant, a leopard and timing built on interruption
titles.essential: The screwball comedy whose pace romantic comedies still borrow.

titles.title: Mr. Smith Goes to Washington
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Original Story
titles.study_note: Capra's idealist against the Senate: a filibuster built from close-ups and reaction shots

titles.title: The Best Years of Our Lives
titles.recognition: Seven Academy Awards, including Best Picture
titles.study_note: Three veterans come home; Gregg Toland's deep focus keeps whole families sharp in one shot, and Harold Russell, who lost his hands in the war, plays a sailor who has too

titles.title: An American in Paris
titles.recognition: Six Academy Awards, including Best Picture
titles.study_note: A 17-minute ballet finale staged in the styles of French painters, in MGM Technicolor
titles.essential: Its ballet finale is the reference for musical numbers built from painting.

titles.title: Top Hat
titles.recognition: Nominated for the Academy Award for Best Picture
titles.study_note: Astaire and Rogers dance "Cheek to Cheek" in long, full-figure takes, on Art Deco sets RKO built white on white

titles.title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone

titles.study_note: Building a world from a book on screen: production design, casting children and a score that became the series' signature

titles.title: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets

titles.title: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban
titles.recognition: Two Academy Award nominations (score and visual effects)
titles.study_note: How a new director changes a series: a moving camera, long takes and a colder palette

titles.title: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire
titles.recognition: Academy Award nomination for art direction
titles.study_note: Set pieces as structure: three tasks, a ball and a graveyard, the tone moving from comedy to dread

titles.title: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix
titles.study_note: Compressing the longest book into the shortest film; a villain written as a bureaucrat

titles.title: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince

titles.title: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows – Part 1

titles.study_note: A road film inside a fantasy series: three actors carrying long stretches alone

titles.title: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows – Part 2

titles.study_note: Paying off ten years of set-ups: a finale built as a siege

titles.title: B.A.P.S.

titles.title: Matilda
titles.study_note: Roald Dahl on screen: grotesque adults shot from a child's eye level

titles.title: The Sound of Music

titles.study_note: Opening on location in the Alps; songs that move the story on rather than pause it

titles.study_note: A family sitcom as a mockumentary: talking heads, three households and cross-cutting

titles.title: Muhammad Ali: The People's Champ
titles.recognition: Opening night film, Urbanworld Film Festival 2015
titles.study_note: Ali's life told through the people he moved, made for BET

titles.title: The College Dropout Video Anthology
titles.study_note: The music videos from Kanye West's first album, with Coodie & Chike's Two Words, Through the Wire and Jesus Walks

titles.study_note: Space projected on screens outside the set's windows, so the actors and the lens saw it for real

titles.title: Inception
titles.recognition: Four Academy Awards: cinematography, visual effects, sound editing and sound mixing

titles.title: Pirates of the Caribbean: At World's End

titles.title: Parasite

titles.title: Skyfall

titles.title: Stranger Things

titles.title: The Green Mile

titles.title: The Godfather Part III
titles.recognition: Seven Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture
titles.study_note: A finale cut against an opera: Gordon Willis's shadows return sixteen years on

titles.title: The Wolf of Wall Street

titles.title: Spider-Man: Homecoming

titles.study_note: A war film with hardly a battle: bunkers, propaganda shoots and a rebellion staged for the camera

titles.title: The Hunger Games: Mockingjay - Part 2
titles.recognition: Over $650 million at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: The Capitol as a booby-trapped city, shot in Berlin and around Paris: the finale as an urban war film

titles.title: The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes
titles.recognition: Over $330 million at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: A prequel 64 years before Katniss: postwar Panem built from Berlin's and Poland's period and brutalist locations

titles.title: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring
titles.recognition: Four Academy Awards, including Best Cinematography
titles.study_note: Peter Jackson shoots all three films back to back in New Zealand: forced perspective, miniatures and Weta's practical makeup

titles.title: The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers
titles.recognition: Two Academy Awards, for visual effects and sound editing
titles.study_note: Gollum, a performance-captured character who carries scenes, and Helm's Deep, shot over months of nights in artificial rain

titles.title: The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King
titles.recognition: Eleven Academy Awards, including Best Picture
titles.study_note: Eleven Oscars from eleven nominations: the Pelennor Fields battle puts crowd-simulation software to work at full scale

titles.title: The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power
titles.study_note: Amazon's Second Age prequel, among the most expensive series ever made: season one shot in New Zealand, season two in the UK

titles.title: The Lord of the Rings: The War of the Rohirrim
titles.study_note: Kenji Kamiyama tells Helm Hammerhand's war as anime, 183 years before the trilogy: Middle-earth drawn by hand

titles.title: The Animatrix
titles.credit: Mahiro Maeda, Shinichiro Watanabe, Peter Chung & others
titles.study_note: Nine animated shorts around the Matrix from anime's leading directors and others: one world in nine visual styles

titles.title: The Matrix Reloaded
titles.recognition: Over $740 million at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: A freeway chase on a mile and a half of road built for it, and the Burly Brawl's crowd of digital doubles

titles.title: The Matrix Revolutions
titles.recognition: Over $425 million at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: Shot back to back with Reloaded: the siege of Zion and a final fight with Agent Smith in pouring rain

titles.title: The Matrix Resurrections
titles.study_note: Lana Wachowski returns 18 years on and writes the franchise's own making into the story: a sequel about sequels

titles.title: Shrek
titles.recognition: The first Academy Award for Best Animated Feature
titles.study_note: DreamWorks' fairy-tale parody and the first Best Animated Feature winner: pop songs, and fur, hair and fire rendered by PDI

titles.title: Shrek 2
titles.credit: Andrew Adamson, Kelly Asbury & Conrad Vernon
titles.recognition: Over $930 million at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: The meet-the-parents sequel, set in Far Far Away, a fairy-tale parody of Hollywood

titles.title: Shrek the Third
titles.recognition: Over $810 million at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: Shrek looks for an heir to the throne: a teenage Arthur, a boarding school and a coup by fairy-tale villains

titles.title: Shrek Forever After
titles.recognition: Over $750 million at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: An alternate world where Shrek was never born: Rumpelstiltskin's kingdom, made for 3D

titles.title: Puss in Boots
titles.recognition: Academy Award nomination for Best Animated Feature
titles.study_note: The spin-off goes back before Shrek: a spaghetti-western origin for the cat, with Humpty Dumpty as his partner

titles.title: Puss in Boots: The Last Wish
titles.recognition: Academy Award nomination for Best Animated Feature
titles.study_note: DreamWorks' painterly turn: fights animated at a choppier frame rate, and a wolf who is Death himself

titles.title: Madagascar
titles.recognition: Over $530 million at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: Four Central Park Zoo animals stranded in the wild: squash-and-stretch animation in the spirit of classic cartoons

titles.title: Madagascar: Escape 2 Africa
titles.recognition: Over $600 million at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: The zoo animals crash-land on the African savanna, where Alex meets the pride he was born into

titles.title: Madagascar 3: Europe's Most Wanted
titles.credit: Eric Darnell, Conrad Vernon & Tom McGrath
titles.recognition: Over $740 million at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: The animals join a travelling circus across Europe: a Monte Carlo chase and a neon trapeze finale

titles.title: Penguins of Madagascar
titles.recognition: Over $370 million at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: The four penguins get their own spy caper against an octopus, with Benedict Cumberbatch's wolf leading a rival agency

titles.title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping
titles.study_note: Francis Lawrence's fifth Hunger Games film goes back 24 years, to the reaping of the 50th Games, from Suzanne Collins's prequel novel

titles.title: The Good Daughter
titles.study_note: Karin Slaughter adapts her own novel and runs the series: two sisters 28 years after one night of violence, pulled back when another attack hits their small town

titles.title: Runner
titles.study_note: A courier has three hours to carry a donor liver from Brisbane to the Gold Coast with a cartel on his tail: Alan Ritchson and Owen Wilson in a race-against-time buddy thriller

titles.title: Never Surrender
titles.study_note: An Indonesian action film: a guilt-ridden veteran and the grandchildren he barely knows hold off a gang at his remote home

titles.title: PAW Patrol: The Dino Movie
titles.recognition: Over $138 million at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: The PAW Patrol's third film strands the pups on a dinosaur island with a volcano about to blow: a preschool series scaled up for the cinema

titles.title: The Invite
titles.recognition: Selected for the Sundance Film Festival
titles.study_note: Olivia Wilde directs a dinner-party comedy: a couple on thin ice invites their upstairs neighbours, and the evening goes somewhere neither expected

titles.title: The Fix
titles.study_note: Disgraced ex-CIA operatives, adrift after the Afghanistan war ends, plan one last score in Tehran

titles.title: The Furious
titles.recognition: Nearly $40 million at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: Action director Kenji Tanigaki's martial-arts thriller: a father hunts for his abducted daughter when corrupt police won't, with Xie Miao and Joe Taslim

titles.title: A Story of Derry
titles.study_note: A half-hour Halloween special from IT: Welcome to Derry, set centuries before Pennywise: three young people go into the Western Wood

titles.title: Apocalypse Z: New World
titles.study_note: The sequel to Apocalypse Z: The Beginning of the End: from the Canary Islands, Europe's last refuge, a mission crosses to the mainland for supplies

titles.title: The Mongoose
titles.study_note: Liam Neeson as a falsely accused war hero leading police on a televised cross-country car chase, with the public rooting for him

titles.title: Avatar: Seven Havens
titles.study_note: The Avatar creators' new animated series: after Korra, a young Earthbender finds she's the Avatar in a world that sees her as its destroyer

titles.title: Kung Fu Soccer
titles.recognition: Over $325 million at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: Stephen Chow returns to football after Shaolin Soccer, this time with a women's team of underdogs out to win the Supreme Invincible Cup

titles.title: Blades of the Guardians
titles.recognition: Over $203 million at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: Yuen Woo-ping, the fight choreographer of The Matrix and Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon, directs a wuxia escort mission across the desert, from a manhua

titles.title: Spider-Noir
titles.study_note: A down-on-his-luck private eye in 1930s New York with a superhero past: Spider-Man as film noir, made in black and white with a full-colour version too

titles.title: Heartland
titles.study_note: A former country music star goes back to Nashville to find out what happened to her rising-star niece

titles.title: The Beast
titles.study_note: Renny Harlin's action thriller: a coup against the United States, fought from inside the president's armoured limousine

titles.title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother
titles.recognition: Selected for the Toronto International Film Festival
titles.study_note: Bassam Tariq (Mogul Mowgli) follows a devout hitman in Houston who, after his wife dies, has to protect his children: faith, fatherhood and crime

titles.title: A Talent for Murder
titles.recognition: Selected for the Toronto International Film Festival
titles.study_note: Anton Corbijn adapts a stage play: a young man visits Patricia Highsmith in Switzerland to persuade her to write one last Ripley novel

titles.title: Widow's Bay
titles.study_note: Katie Dippold's comedy horror series: a New England island's mayor wants tourists, and the locals insist the place is cursed

titles.title: Milk
titles.recognition: Academy Awards for Best Actor (Sean Penn) and Original Screenplay
titles.study_note: Gus Van Sant restages Harvey Milk's San Francisco on Castro Street itself, cutting real news footage of the time into the drama

titles.title: The Lion King
titles.recognition: Over $1.6 billion at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: Jon Favreau shoots a fully computer-made film like a live-action one: the crew worked real camera rigs, cranes and dollies inside virtual reality

titles.title: X2
titles.recognition: Over $407 million at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: Opens on Nightcrawler teleporting through the White House, one of the sequel's set pieces built from practical sets and visual effects together

titles.title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
titles.recognition: Over $745 million at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: Two casts playing the same characters decades apart, the 1973 scenes and a dark future cut together around Quicksilver's slow-motion kitchen sequence

titles.title: Logan
titles.recognition: Academy Award nominee, Best Adapted Screenplay
titles.study_note: James Mangold makes his superhero film a western: dusty roads, an old man and a girl, and a black-and-white cut released as Logan Noir

titles.title: Doctor Zhivago
titles.recognition: Five Academy Awards, including Best Adapted Screenplay and Cinematography
titles.study_note: David Lean's Russian epic was shot mostly in Spain, its winters made with fake snow and its frozen house dressed in wax

titles.title: Wednesday
titles.recognition: Netflix's most-watched English-language series
titles.study_note: Tim Burton directs four of the first eight episodes, shot in Romania, and Jenna Ortega choreographed Wednesday's dance herself

titles.title: Beauty and the Beast
titles.recognition: Over $1.2 billion at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: Disney's 1991 animation remade in live action, with Dan Stevens on stilts in a motion-capture suit for the Beast and his face captured separately

titles.title: X-Men: The Last Stand
titles.recognition: Over $459 million at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: The trilogy's finale is built around a cure for mutation, ending with the Golden Gate Bridge torn loose and swung to Alcatraz

titles.title: Everything Everywhere All at Once
titles.recognition: Seven Academy Awards, including Best Picture and Director
titles.study_note: The Daniels made a multiverse on a modest budget, with a visual-effects team of five artists working mostly from home

titles.title: The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Makeup
titles.study_note: Andrew Adamson, coming from Shrek, shot in New Zealand and set a computer-made Aslan among real snowfields and forests

titles.title: American Psycho
titles.recognition: Premiered at the Sundance Film Festival
titles.study_note: Mary Harron plays Bret Easton Ellis's killer as satire: 1980s Manhattan offices, business cards and restaurant bookings shot as straight-faced as an advert

titles.title: The Expendables
titles.recognition: Over $274 million at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: Sylvester Stallone directs and gathers a generation of action stars, with Jason Statham, Jet Li, Dolph Lundgren and a scene with Bruce Willis and Arnold Schwarzenegger

titles.title: Octopussy
titles.recognition: Over $187 million at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: Roger Moore's Bond in Udaipur, with an auto-rickshaw chase through the streets, a palace on Lake Pichola and a fight on top of a moving train

titles.title: House of Cards
titles.recognition: Netflix's first original drama series; Emmy Award for David Fincher's direction of its first episode
titles.study_note: David Fincher sets the look in the first two episodes: still, symmetrical frames, a cold palette and a lead who speaks straight to camera

titles.title: The Crown
titles.recognition: Emmy Award for Outstanding Drama Series, 2021
titles.study_note: Peter Morgan recasts the royal family every two seasons, so three actresses play Elizabeth II across six decades

titles.title: Sex Education
titles.recognition: BAFTA TV Award for Aimee Lou Wood, 2021
titles.study_note: Shot in Wales and styled like an American high-school film: letterman jackets, lockers and a bright palette at a British school

titles.title: Stargate
titles.recognition: Over $196 million at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: Roland Emmerich builds an ancient Egypt on another planet in the dunes of the American desert: the film that started a television franchise

titles.title: A View to a Kill
titles.recognition: Duran Duran's theme reached number one in the United States
titles.study_note: Roger Moore's last Bond: a parachute jump from the Eiffel Tower and a finale on the Golden Gate Bridge

titles.title: In Bruges
titles.recognition: Academy Award nominee, Best Original Screenplay
titles.study_note: Martin McDonagh's first feature, shot on location: two hitmen killing time in a medieval town that plays as a third character

titles.title: Dallas Buyers Club
titles.recognition: Three Academy Awards, including Best Actor (Matthew McConaughey) and Supporting Actor (Jared Leto)
titles.study_note: Shot in about a month on a small budget, handheld and without film lights, by Jean-Marc Vallée

titles.title: Fifty Shades of Grey
titles.recognition: Over $569 million at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: Sam Taylor-Johnson, a photographer and video artist, adapts E. L. James's bestseller with Seamus McGarvey's cool, glossy cinematography

titles.title: Cinderella
titles.recognition: Over $542 million at the worldwide box office; Academy Award nominee, Best Costume Design
titles.study_note: Kenneth Branagh plays the fairy tale straight, with Sandy Powell's costumes and a palace built on the stages at Pinewood

titles.title: Licence to Kill
titles.recognition: Over $156 million at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: Timothy Dalton's darker Bond, out for revenge, shot largely in Mexico and ending in a tanker-truck chase down a mountain road

titles.title: Mutiny on the Bounty
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Picture
titles.study_note: MGM sailed full-size replicas of the Bounty and the Pandora off Catalina Island, with Charles Laughton and Clark Gable

titles.title: Saw II
titles.recognition: Over $147 million at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: Made for about $4 million, with a cast locked in one booby-trapped house: Darren Lynn Bousman's first feature

titles.title: 3:10 to Yuma
titles.recognition: Two Academy Award nominations
titles.study_note: James Mangold remakes the 1957 western on New Mexico locations, with Russell Crowe and Christian Bale

titles.title: The Danish Girl
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress (Alicia Vikander)
titles.study_note: Tom Hooper and cinematographer Danny Cohen take their frames from painting, especially Vilhelm Hammershøi's quiet Copenhagen interiors

titles.title: Onward
titles.recognition: Academy Award nominee, Best Animated Feature
titles.study_note: Pixar's suburban fantasy road trip, drawn from Dan Scanlon losing his father when he was a baby

titles.title: Grand Hotel
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Picture
titles.study_note: MGM's stars under one Berlin hotel roof, with Greta Garbo, John and Lionel Barrymore and Joan Crawford: the model for every ensemble hotel film since

titles.title: The Broadway Melody
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Picture
titles.study_note: MGM's first all-talking musical and the first sound film to win Best Picture, with one number shot in two-strip Technicolor

titles.title: Lord of War
titles.study_note: Andrew Niccol's arms-dealer satire opens on one bullet's life from factory to gunshot, and the production used real guns and tanks because they cost less than props

titles.title: One Battle After Another
titles.study_note: Paul Thomas Anderson shoots in VistaVision, the 1950s widescreen film format, with Leonardo DiCaprio as a burnt-out revolutionary, loosely from Thomas Pynchon's Vineland

titles.title: Alice Through the Looking Glass
titles.recognition: Over $299 million at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: James Bobin follows Tim Burton's Alice into a sequel built largely on blue screen, with Sacha Baron Cohen as Time

titles.title: Thelma & Louise
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay (Callie Khouri)
titles.study_note: Ridley Scott's road movie across the American Southwest, filmed largely in Utah's canyon country and ending on its famous freeze-frame

titles.title: Roma
titles.recognition: Academy Awards for Best Director, Cinematography and Foreign Language Film; Venice Golden Lion
titles.study_note: Alfonso Cuarón shot it himself, in black-and-white on large-format digital cameras, with slow pans across the 1970s Mexico City of his childhood

titles.title: Divergent
titles.recognition: Over $288 million at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: Neil Burger sets Veronica Roth's young-adult dystopia in a walled-in, half-ruined Chicago, filmed on the city's real streets and trains

titles.title: The Expendables 2
titles.recognition: Over $314 million at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: Simon West takes over from Sylvester Stallone and shoots in Bulgaria, adding Jean-Claude Van Damme and Chuck Norris to the line-up

titles.title: Anora
titles.recognition: Palme d'Or; five Academy Awards, including Best Picture
titles.study_note: Sean Baker shot on 35mm on a small budget in Brighton Beach and Las Vegas, and edited the film himself

titles.title: Contagion
titles.recognition: Over $136 million at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: Steven Soderbergh shot it himself under the name Peter Andrews, following a pandemic through hands, door handles and glasses

titles.title: The Chronicles of Narnia: Prince Caspian
titles.recognition: Over $419 million at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: Andrew Adamson's sequel, filmed in New Zealand, the Czech Republic, Slovenia and Poland, around a night raid on a castle built for it

titles.title: Narcos
titles.credit: Chris Brancato, Carlo Bernard & Doug Miro
titles.recognition: Golden Globe nominations for Best Drama Series and for Wagner Moura
titles.study_note: Shot on location in Colombia, in English and Spanish, with a DEA agent's voice-over cut against real archive footage of Pablo Escobar's era

titles.title: Don't Look Up
titles.recognition: Four Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture
titles.study_note: Adam McKay's comet satire with Leonardo DiCaprio and Jennifer Lawrence, filmed in Massachusetts under pandemic safety rules

titles.title: Sicario
titles.recognition: Three Academy Award nominations, including Best Cinematography
titles.study_note: Roger Deakins shoots the border from above and at night, including a raid seen through thermal and night-vision cameras

titles.title: 21 Grams
titles.recognition: Academy Award nominations for Naomi Watts and Benicio del Toro
titles.study_note: Guillermo Arriaga's script is told out of order, and Rodrigo Prieto shot it handheld with heavy grain and drained colour

titles.title: Hulk
titles.recognition: Over $245 million at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: Ang Lee cuts the film like comic-book panels, with split screens and wipes across the frame

titles.title: Darkest Hour
titles.recognition: Academy Awards for Best Actor (Gary Oldman) and Makeup and Hairstyling
titles.study_note: Gary Oldman becomes Churchill under Kazu Hiro's prosthetics, in a London lit by shafts of light through bunker and Parliament windows

titles.title: Wonder Woman 1984
titles.recognition: Released in cinemas and on HBO Max on the same day
titles.study_note: Patty Jenkins sets the sequel in 1984, restoring a shopping mall of the era inside a real Virginia mall

titles.title: Cruella
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Costume Design (Jenny Beavan)
titles.study_note: Jenny Beavan's costumes take 101 Dalmatians' villain into 1970s London punk and couture

titles.title: Mrs. Miniver
titles.recognition: Six Academy Awards, including Best Picture
titles.study_note: Made in Hollywood while Britain was at war, its English village built on MGM's lot; its closing sermon was printed as leaflets and dropped over Europe

titles.title: Hannibal
titles.recognition: Over $351 million at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: Ridley Scott moves Hannibal Lecter to Florence, filming in its palazzos, piazzas and museums

titles.title: Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time
titles.recognition: Over $336 million at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: Adapted from the video game and filmed in Morocco's deserts, with free-running stunts across rooftops

titles.title: Enchanted
titles.recognition: Three Academy Award nominations for Best Original Song
titles.study_note: Disney sends a hand-drawn princess into live-action New York: the film starts in traditional animation and steps out into Central Park

titles.title: Tron: Legacy
titles.recognition: Over $400 million at the worldwide box office
titles.study_note: Joseph Kosinski lit the Grid with light built into the suits and sets, to a score by Daft Punk

titles.title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Film Editing
titles.study_note: David Fincher shoots Stieg Larsson's thriller in a Swedish winter, in a cold, drained palette, to Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross's score

titles.title: Cat on a Hot Tin Roof
titles.recognition: Six Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture
titles.study_note: Tennessee Williams's play on screen, with Elizabeth Taylor and Paul Newman, kept almost entirely inside one Mississippi plantation house

titles.title: The Great Ziegfeld
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Picture
titles.study_note: MGM's three-hour biography of the Broadway showman, built around a revolving, wedding-cake set for 'A Pretty Girl Is Like a Melody'

titles.title: Daredevil
titles.study_note: Netflix's first Marvel series, with a hallway fight in its second episode played as one unbroken take

titles.title: The Witcher
titles.study_note: Adapted from Andrzej Sapkowski's Polish novels and filmed in Hungary and on the Canary Islands, with Henry Cavill as Geralt for three seasons

titles.title: The Queen's Gambit
titles.recognition: Emmy Award for Outstanding Limited Series, 2021
titles.study_note: Scott Frank's limited series about a chess prodigy, filmed in Berlin standing in for 1950s and 60s Kentucky, Paris, Mexico City and Moscow
